name: Is it safe to publish AI-generated FAQs about my services without a human reviewing them?

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to publish AI-generated FAQs about my services without a human reviewing them?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, but review is essential when answers involve regulated, technical, safety-sensitive, or highly consequential decisions. AI can help organize questions and draft explanations, but unsupported claims, outdated details, and missing exceptions can damage trust.

Context: AI Visibility Solutions describes research and automated publishing workflows, yet business-specific facts still require approval from the knowledgeable owner or qualified subject-matter reviewer. Google also emphasizes helpful, reliable, people-first content.

Key factors:
- Whether facts change frequently.
- Whether the answer depends on customer-specific conditions.
- Whether the page could be interpreted as a guarantee.
- Who owns corrections after publication.

Practical guidance: Create an approval checklist, record source dates, mark uncertainty or conditions clearly, and schedule reviews for time-sensitive pages. Do not publish automatically when an expert review is reasonably required.

Human oversight protects accuracy while automation improves scale.
acceptedAnswer.description: No. AI-generated FAQs need human review for accuracy, limits, outdated facts, and customer-specific exceptions—especially for technical, regulated, safety-sensitive, or consequential topics. Maintain an approval process and review schedule before publishing or updating pages.
